title: BDL Basic Circular No. 171: Requests by the Banque du Liban and/or the Banking Control Commission of Lebanon to Lift Banking Secrecy
text:
Basic Circular No. 171
Addressed to Banks and Institutions Regulated by the Banque du Liban
Attached is a copy of Basic Decision No. 13768 of 14 November 2025, on Requests by the
Banque du Liban and/or the Banking Control Commission of Lebanon to Lift Banking
Secrecy.
Beirut, 14 November 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid

Basic Decision No. 13768
Requests by the Banque du Liban and/or the Banking Control Commission of Lebanon
to Lift Banking Secrecy
The Governor of the Banque du Liban,
Pursuant to the Code of Money and Credit, in particular Article 150 thereof;
Pursuant to Article 7 of the Law of 3 September 1956 on Banking Secrecy;
Pursuant to Decree No. 1578 of 15 October 2025; and
Pursuant to the Decision of the Central Council of the Banque du Liban taken in its
meeting of 12 November 2025,
Decides the following:
Article 1:
All banks and institutions regulated by the Banque du Liban are bound to respond to the
requests to lift banking secrecy sent by the Banque du Liban (BDL) and/or the Banking
Control Commission of Lebanon (BCCL), without invoking any argument or excuse of any
kind.
Article 2:
The requests to lift banking secrecy referred to in Article 1 above shall include the inquiry
about any registers, documents, and information pertaining to a legal entity or natural person
that deals with any bank or institution regulated by the BDL. Retroactive information may be
requested, on condition that it does not go beyond ten years from the issuance date of Law
No. 1 of 24 April 2025.
Article 3:
First: Requests shall be sent, either electronically in an encrypted and secured form, or in
writing in a confidential and secured form, to the Board Chairperson or the General
Director of any bank or institution regulated by the BDL, provided that the requests
clearly indicate the information and data under investigation.
1

Second: The request of the Banque du Liban shall be signed by the Governor of the Banque
du Liban or by the person delegated by the Governor for that purpose, and the
request of the Banking Control Commission of Lebanon shall be signed by the
BCCL Chairperson or the person delegated by the Chairperson for that purpose.
Auditors or valuers appointed by the BDL or the BCCL may request the
information referred to in Article 2 above, as per the tasks assigned to them. They
shall provide the BDL or the BCCL, depending on whom appointed them, with a
specific preliminary request to be attached to the request of the BDL and/or the
BCCL.
Article 4:
The Board Chairperson or the General Director of the concerned bank or institution must
adopt an appropriate mechanism that identifies:
- The persons in charge of reading and examining incoming requests, among which the
Head of the Compliance Unit (at the concerned bank) or the Compliance Officer at
the concerned institution.
- The necessary measures to be followed to respond to these requests, particularly in
terms of sending the requested information through secured channels such as the
encrypted email.
- The precautionary measures to be taken to preserve the confidentiality of the
information and prevent their falling into the hands of third parties.
Article 5:
First: Documents sent to the BDL and/or the BCCL must be stamped with the expression
“Confidential”.
Second: The receipt of the information and documents requested by the BDL or the BCCL
must be confirmed.
Third: The concerned bank or institution must maintain a record with the transfer details
of the required information and documents, and must make sure that they were
received by the BDL or the BCCL. This information must be kept in the concerned
institution’s records for at least ten years.
Article 6:
Each bank and institution regulated by the Banque du Liban must respond to the BDL and the
BCCL requests referred to in this Basic Decision, within a maximum time limit of 15
business days from the date on which they have received these requests.
2

Article 7:
Any violation of the provisions of this Decision shall expose the violating bank or institution
to the sanctions specified in applicable laws and regulations, particularly the provisions of
Article 208 of the Code of Money and Credit.
Article 8:
The Banking Control Commission of Lebanon shall monitor the implementation of the
provisions of this Decision, and shall specify, if necessary, the implementation measures
needed to update and develop a mechanism for information exchange with concerned banks
and institutions.
Article 9:
This Decision shall come into force upon its issuance.
Article 10:
This Decision shall be published in the Official Gazette.
Beirut, 14 November 2025
The Governor of the Banque du Liban
Karim Souaid
3
